irregularities.title: Contest rules differ sharply on whether an AI coding agent may do the work
irregularities.summary: Winning Writers prohibits AI-generated text; ESPN prohibits automated entry programs; CBS may disqualify automated scripts; ARC Prize forbids internet/API models during evaluation and requires open-sourced code; TradingView warns that scripts can trigger bans. Conversely, the Codex x TwitchCon rules require Codex and permit AI coding assistants, the Global Virtual Hackathon says AI tools are 'allowed and expected', and Metaculus runs a bot-only tournament.
evidence: 'may not contain any AI-generated text'
'Entries must be manually key-stroked by the entrant; use of automated entry devices or programs ... are prohibited.'
'accumulating points through methods such as automated computer scripts'
'Internet access is not available during Kaggle evaluation (no API-based systems like GPT/Claude/etc.)'
'Building with AI tools is allowed and expected.'
'This is a bot-only competition where bot-makers attempt to push AI to its limits'
irregularities.action: A dedicated AI-agent compatibility table on the Analysis page quotes each rule with its official link; no contest is described as agent-friendly without that quote.

irregularities.title: GEMS Prize official rules and competition homepage disagree on the submission cut-off time, and AI use must be disclosed
irregularities.summary: The DrivenData competition page says submissions close 'Dec. 3, 2026, 11:59 p.m. UTC'. The September 2026 official rules (Appendix A.1) say the final content must be posted 'by 5:00 p.m. ET on the prize submission deadline date'. Section 3.2 permits generative AI but requires a narrative disclosure of the extent and manner of use. Section 3.1 states how to enter but no fee amount, so free entry is not confirmed.
evidence: '### Dec. 3, 2026, 11:59 p.m. UTC' (competition homepage)

'You must post the final content of your submission or upload the submission form online by 5:00 p.m. ET on the prize submission deadline date before the prize's phase submission period closes.' (official rules A.1)

'Using generative AI technology in the development of your prize submission is allowed. However, you must indicate in the narrative ... the extent to which, if any, you used generative AI technology and how you used it' (official rules 3.2)
'To enter the competition, you must create a profile on the DrivenData platform and agree to abide by the competition rules and restrictions.' (official rules 3.1)
irregularities.action: Both times are published with their source links; no reconciled deadline is invented. The verified deadline cell keeps the competition homepage's date and links to it, while the conflict is flagged here. Generative-AI disclosure is quoted on the row and the Analysis page. Handed off by session 4db3cf09-own1 in PR #3; re-verified against the official rules on 2026-11-02.

irregularities.title: Metaculus tournament rules bar bots and AI accounts from prizes by default
irregularities.summary: The platform-wide rules say automated systems, bots, artificial intelligence and registered bot accounts are ineligible for tournament prizes unless competition-specific rules permit them. Human participants may use AI tools only when final submissions reflect their own decisions and understanding. The FutureEval Bot Tournament is therefore an explicit exception, not a general permission.
evidence: 'Unless otherwise specifically permitted in the Competition-specific rules, automated systems, bots, artificial intelligence, or user accounts which are officially registered as bot accounts, are ineligible for tournament prizes.'
'However, human participants are allowed to use AI tools or systems to assist in their forecasting, as long as the final submissions reflect their own decisions and understanding.'
'No purchase, fee, or payment is required to participate.'
'Any person wishing to participate must create a free Metaculus user account. No purchase or entry fee is necessary to enter a Metaculus competition.'
irregularities.action: The platform rule is quoted on the Analysis page and on the Metaculus detail page; the bot-only tournament is listed as a competition-specific exception. Requested by session 4db3cf09-own1 in PR #3; independently re-verified on the official rules page on 2026-11-02.
